narrative: Eight months of interlocking faults (seat resets, alert config not saving, export/API truncation) recurred repeatedly despite being marked resolved each time, prompting a formal escalation in June 2025 ('I want to escalate formally'). This is real recovery, not a quiet lull - the account is re-engaging, not disengaging.

A fiscal-year dashboard bug recurs three times ('That is not acceptable for a BI platform'), and an API credentials access request from October 2024 was never confirmed resolved. This account is stating its exit criteria in writing.

Impatience shows across threads ('Please fix properly this time, not just resend'; 'appreciate a fix rather than an apology') but this reads as an engaged customer working the product hard, not one drifting toward the door - nothing stays unresolved.

Alerts failed three separate times over six months, culminating in 'I have no confidence in this feature at this point,' and a September ERP connector complaint - explicitly asking for 'a root cause analysis, not another temporary workaround' - was never followed up on and stays unresolved. Consistently positive, low-friction account: quick seat provisioning, connector migration help, and a roadmap suggestion, ending with unprompted confirmation that shared dashboard links have been working smoothly for weeks. No unresolved issues and no complaints of substance.

competitor_mentions.quote: As part of our tooling review this year we've also been asked to take a look at Dashlume as an alternative, mainly to compare API flexibility, so it would help to understand the scope model properly either way.

narrative: The textbook quiet-risk pattern: recurring formatting and permission bugs (SSO tier mapping, report builder column order, dashboard filter persistence) get marked resolved but keep resurfacing, and the customer now builds manual workarounds and time buffers rather than chasing fixes ('just noting it here for completeness rather than expecting a fix ahead of anything else in the queue'). Layered on top is a serious competitor signal - the account is formally evaluating Dashlume as part of a tooling review while comparing API flexibility. Quiet resignation plus an active competitor evaluation is a worse combination than any single loud complaint.
